raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
> Apertus-v1.5-8B is not in upstream SGLang yet (#32979), so its rows below were measured with this same change on [swiss-ai/sglang-apertus `apertus-1-5`](https://github.com/swiss-ai/sglang-apertus/pull/4), with transformers [swiss-ai@3797303](https://github.com/swiss-ai/transformers/tree/3797303dda74844e3d1f8977ff5518bb91f818b4) as pinned by the model card. Apertus-8B-Instruct-2509 rows are on upstream `main`.

## Motivation

Apertus's MLP is `up_proj -> xIELU -> down_proj` on a `[tokens, 21504]` tensor (8B). Today `XIELU` runs one of two paths:

- If the optional [nickjbrowning/XIELU](https://github.com/nickjbrowning/XIELU) package is installed, its CUDA kernel. It is not a dependency, has to be built from source (on torch 2.14 it also needs `-std=c++20`, and its CMake sets no CUDA architecture), and SGLang calls it with `with_vector_loads=False`.
- Otherwise a bf16 `torch.where` expression of about ten elementwise kernels.

Both evaluate in bf16 with bf16 coefficients. With the checkpoints' large layer-0 coefficients (`softplus(alpha_p) ≈ 166`, `alpha_n ≈ 41` in Apertus-8B-Instruct-2509) the negative branch cancels near `x ≈ -0.024`, and about half of all outputs are not correctly rounded.

## Modifications

- `kernels/jit/csrc/elementwise/xielu.cuh`, `kernels/ops/activation/xielu.py`: a JIT xIELU kernel (fp16/bf16). It evaluates the fp32 expression with explicitly rounded operations (no FMA contraction), in the order of the torch reference, and rounds once. The launcher picks the widest vector (up to `kMaxVecBytes`) that both buffers are aligned to and that still leaves `SM count x 512` threads: at decode sizes the per-element `expm1f` is latency-bound, so fewer elements per thread wins. A thread past the last vector handles the tail. PDL as in the other activation kernels. Registered as `activation.xielu`, and as a custom op so `torch.compile` sees it as opaque.
- `XIELU`: the effective coefficients `[softplus(alpha_p), beta + softplus(alpha_n), beta, eps]` live in a non-persistent fp32 buffer `_coeffs`, derived with torch ops by `update_coefficients()` and read by the kernel on device. This keeps the layer constructible on the meta device (zero-copy IPC loading), lets the IPC daemon's exported buffers carry the loaded values, and lets captured CUDA graphs follow in-place weight updates. Inputs other than fp16/bf16 (e.g. `--dtype float32`) and non-contiguous inputs use the native fp32 expression. The optional external package path, its 3-D reshape warning and the dynamo special case are removed.
- `ApertusForCausalLM`: calls `update_coefficients` after `load_weights` and from `post_load_weights`. This also replaces the old path's `beta`/`eps` scalars, which were cached at construction rather than from the checkpoint.

## Accuracy Tests

Outputs not correctly rounded vs float64 truth from each checkpoint's own coefficients, `[4096, 21504]` N(0, 1.5²) bf16 inputs:

| checkpoint, layer | torch expression | package (as SGLang calls it) | package, `with_vector_loads=True` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Apertus-8B-Instruct-2509, 0 | 49.3% (max 35,622 ulp) | 51.7% (max 8,371 ulp) | 47.9% (max 491,738 ulp) | 0.00% (max 1 ulp) |
| Apertus-8B-Instruct-2509, 15 | 54.5% | 55.7% | 57.2% | 0.00% |
| Apertus-8B-Instruct-2509, 31 | 48.7% | 52.9% | 53.9% | 0.00% |
| Apertus-v1.5-8B, 0 | 47.5% (max 24,759 ulp) | 52.2% (max 2,177 ulp) | 51.2% (max 65,353 ulp) | 0.00% (max 1 ulp) |
| Apertus-v1.5-8B, 15 | 55.8% | 61.0% | 61.5% | 0.00% |
| Apertus-v1.5-8B, 31 | 47.7% | 55.3% | 56.8% | 0.00% |

GSM8K (all 1319, greedy, `sglang.test.run_eval`):

| checkpoint | torch expression | package | package (vec) | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Apertus-8B-Instruct-2509 | 0.616 | 0.609 | **0.000** (empty completions) | **0.626** |
| Apertus-v1.5-8B | 0.798 | 0.803 | 0.788 | **0.807** |

For reference, the Apertus tech report lists 62.9 for Apertus-8B-Instruct-2509 (8-shot CoT, a different harness); no per-benchmark GSM8K has been published for 1.5. The vectorised package path breaking 1.0 but not 1.5 matches the accuracy table: its worst error on 1.0's layer 0 is 7.5x larger.

The kernel is bit-identical to the fp32 torch reference in bf16 for every one of the 65,536 bit patterns. In fp16 it is within 1 ulp: the toolkit's `expm1f` can differ by one ulp from torch's, which the cancellation exposes on 10 of 65,536 inputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

RTX 5090 (SM120), torch 2.14.1+cu130, CUDA 13.2, bf16, CUDA graphs, all jobs serialised on the GPU.

Kernel, `[M, 21504]` bf16, Apertus-8B-Instruct-2509 layer-0 coefficients, µs per call (CUDA-graph replays, cold L2, arms interleaved in random order, 60 rounds); speedup = median paired ratio [95% bootstrap CI]:

| M | torch expression | package | package (vec) | this PR | vs package |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15.08 | 0.75 | 1.00 | 0.49 | 1.52x [1.52, 1.52] |
| 16 | 17.13 | 1.52 | 1.26 | 1.21 | 1.25x [1.20, 1.45] |
| 64 | 27.37 | 3.05 | 2.28 | 1.83 | 1.67x [1.51, 1.72] |
| 128 | 41.90 | 5.10 | 3.82 | 3.30 | 1.54x [1.54, 1.54] |
| 1024 | 541.7 | 65.4 | 34.7 | 18.3 | 3.58x [3.47, 3.58] |
| 4096 | 3259 | 297.6 | 225.1 | 208.7 | 1.42x [1.42, 1.43] |
| 8192 | 6536 | 597.9 | 463.7 | 440.2 | 1.36x [1.36, 1.36] |

At M = 4096 the kernel moves 1.69 TB/s (94% of the card's 1.79 TB/s DRAM peak). Reading the coefficients on device (second commit) costs nothing: in a same-process A/B against float arguments it is 1.00–1.09x as fast at every M.

End to end, `sglang.Engine`, fixed lengths, greedy, `ignore_eos`, radix cache off, fresh random prompts per repeat; mean over 2 launches × 3 repeats (arms interleaved, launch order reversed):

| checkpoint | scenario | torch expression | package | package (vec) | this PR | vs torch | vs package |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8B-Instruct-2509 | batch 1, 512/256, out tok/s | 95.6 | 100.3 | 100.2 | 100.4 | +5.0% | +0.1% |
| 8B-Instruct-2509 | batch 32, 512/256, out tok/s | 1,703.6 | 1,916.3 | 1,921.9 | 1,921.8 | +12.8% | +0.3% |
| 8B-Instruct-2509 | prefill 32 × 4096, in tok/s | 10,223 | 13,199 | 13,272 | 13,286 | +30.0% | +0.7% |
| v1.5-8B | batch 1, 512/256, out tok/s | 94.4 | 100.2 | 100.2 | 100.2 | +6.1% | +0.0% |
| v1.5-8B | batch 32, 512/256, out tok/s | 1,687.5 | 1,918.5 | 1,924.1 | 1,925.8 | +14.1% | +0.4% |
| v1.5-8B | prefill 32 × 4096, in tok/s | 10,136 | 13,218 | 13,284 | 13,267 | +30.9% | +0.4% |

95% CIs are within ±0.2% for every arm except the torch expression (up to ±1.2%). Re-running this PR's arm on the final code gives the same throughput within 0.3% on both checkpoints.

So this matches the package end to end (the activation is ~1% of a step once it is one kernel) without the external build or its numerics, and is 5–31% faster than what runs when the package is absent.

## Review

Two findings from a Codex review were fixed in the second commit: `.item()` in `XIELU.__init__` broke meta-device construction (zero-copy IPC loading), and float32 inputs reached the fp16/bf16-only kernel. A re-review of the fix found nothing further.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (`pre-commit run --all-files`; the Rust hooks were skipped locally for lack of a toolchain, and no Rust is touched.)
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). `test/registered/kernels/ops/activation/test_xielu.py`, 41 cases passing on an RTX 5090: every bit pattern, shapes covering each vector width, odd tails, misaligned views, special values, `out=`, empty input, a CUDA graph following an in-place coefficient update, the layer's coefficient derivation with native/CUDA agreement, the float32 fallback, and meta-device construction. `test/registered/unit/kernels/` and `test/registered/unit/models/test_kv_calibration_loader_layout.py` also pass.
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing change.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Note on the removed package path

`with_vector_loads=True` on the package makes Apertus-8B-Instruct-2509 return empty completions (GSM8K 0.000), and the scalar path SGLang uses is matched end to end by this kernel with correctly rounded outputs. So I removed the optional import rather than keeping it as a fallback; happy to keep it behind a flag if you prefer.

files.patch:
@@ -153,6 +153,16 @@ def situ_and_mul(
 )
 
 
+register_kernel(
+    KernelSpec(
+        op="activation.xielu",
+        backend=KernelBackend.JIT,
+        target="sglang.kernels.ops.activation.xielu:xielu",
+        capabilities=CUDA_ONLY,
+    )
+)
+
+
 # Kernels introduced with Kimi-K3, inventoried by logical operator group.
 register_kernel(
     KernelSpec(

@@ -0,0 +1,82 @@
+"""xIELU activation (https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.13010), used by Apertus."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Optional
+
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils import (
+    cache_once,
+    is_arch_support_pdl,
+    load_jit,
+    make_cpp_args,
+)
+from sglang.srt.utils.custom_op import register_custom_op
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from tvm_ffi.module import Module
+
+
+@cache_once
+def _jit_xielu_module(dtype: torch.dtype) -> Module:
+    if dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
+        raise RuntimeError(f"xielu supports float16 and bfloat16, got {dtype}")
+    args = make_cpp_args(dtype, is_arch_support_pdl())
+    return load_jit(
+        "xielu",
+        *args,
+        cuda_files=["elementwise/xielu.cuh"],
+        cuda_wrappers=[("xielu", f"XIELUKernel<{args}>::run")],
+    )
+
+
+@register_custom_op(mutates_args=["out"])
+def _xielu_inplace(
+    input: torch.Tensor, out: torch.Tensor, coeffs: torch.Tensor
+) -> None:
+    _jit_xielu_module(input.dtype).xielu(input.view(-1), out.view(-1), coeffs)
+
+
+def xielu(
+    input: torch.Tensor, coeffs: torch.Tensor, out: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Elementwise xIELU on a contiguous float16/bfloat16 CUDA tensor.
+
+    ``coeffs`` is the fp32 tensor from :func:`xielu_coeffs` on the same device.
+    The expression is evaluated in fp32 and rounded once, bit-identical to
+    :func:`xielu_reference` in bfloat16.
+    """
+    if out is None:
+        out = torch.empty_like(input)
+    _xielu_inplace(input, out, coeffs)
+    return out
+
+
+def xielu_coeffs(
+    alpha_p: torch.Tensor,
+    alpha_n: torch.Tensor,
+    beta: torch.Tensor,
+    eps: torch.Tensor,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Effective coefficients from the checkpoint's pre-softplus parameters, as
+    fp32 ``[softplus(alpha_p), beta + softplus(alpha_n), beta, eps]``."""
+    beta = beta.float().reshape(1)
+    return torch.cat(
+        [
+            F.softplus(alpha_p.float()).reshape(1),
+            beta + F.softplus(alpha_n.float()).reshape(1),
+            beta,
+            eps.float().reshape(1),
+        ]
+    )
+
+
+def xielu_reference(x: torch.Tensor, coeffs: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """The fp32 torch expression the kernel matches, rounded once to ``x.dtype``."""
+    alpha_p, alpha_n, beta, eps = coeffs.to(x.device).unbind()
+    xf = x.float()
+    pos = alpha_p * xf * xf + beta * xf
+    neg = (torch.expm1(torch.clamp_max(xf, eps)) - xf) * alpha_n + beta * xf
+    return torch.where(xf > 0, pos, neg).to(x.dtype)

@@ -23,6 +23,7 @@
 from transformers import PretrainedConfig
 
 from sglang.kernels.fused_op import BaseFusedOp
+from sglang.kernels.ops.activation.xielu import xielu_coeffs, xielu_reference
 from sglang.srt.distributed import (
     divide,
 )
@@ -73,6 +74,7 @@
     from sglang.kernels.ops.activation.activation import (
         silu_and_mul as _jit_silu_and_mul,

+import sys
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils import get_ci_test_range
+from sglang.kernels.ops.activation.xielu import xielu, xielu_coeffs, xielu_reference
+from sglang.srt.layers.activation import XIELU
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=15, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+# Nightly is not redundant here: it sets SGLANG_JIT_KERNEL_RUN_FULL_TESTS=1 to expand get_ci_test_range sweeps.
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=15, stage="nightly", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+# Post-softplus coefficients of layer 0 of swiss-ai/Apertus-8B-Instruct-2509. Its large
+# alpha_n makes the negative branch cancel near x = -2 * beta / alpha_n, which is where
+# lower-precision evaluations go wrong.
+COEFFS = torch.tensor([166.0, 41.25, 0.5, -9.98377799987793e-07], device="cuda")
+DTYPES = [torch.bfloat16, torch.float16]
+# Apertus's MLP width is 21504; the row counts cover every vector width the launcher
+# picks, from decode batches to prefill chunks.
+SHAPES = get_ci_test_range(
+    full_range=[(m, 21504) for m in (1, 2, 3, 16, 31, 64, 128, 1024, 4096)]
+    + [(1,), (7,), (17,), (1000003,), (2, 5, 1000)],
+    ci_range=[(1, 21504), (16, 21504), (128, 21504), (1024, 21504), (17,)],
+)
+
+
+def _bits(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return x.view(torch.int16).int()
+
+
+def _assert_matches(out: torch.Tensor, ref: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+    """bf16 must be bit-identical. In fp16 the expm1f of the CUDA toolkit can differ by
+    one ulp from torch's, which shows up after the cancellation, so allow one ulp."""
+    assert out.shape == ref.shape and out.dtype == ref.dtype
+    both_nan = out.isnan() & ref.isnan()
+    assert torch.equal(out.isnan(), ref.isnan())
+    diff = torch.where(both_nan, 0, (_bits(out) - _bits(ref)).abs())
+    limit = 0 if out.dtype == torch.bfloat16 else 1
+    assert diff.numel() == 0 or diff.max().item() <= limit, diff.max().item()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", DTYPES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("shape", SHAPES)
+def test_xielu_matches_fp32_reference(dtype: torch.dtype, shape: tuple) -> None:
+    x = (torch.randn(shape, device="cuda") * 3).to(dtype)
+    _assert_matches(xielu(x, COEFFS), xielu_reference(x, COEFFS))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", DTYPES)
+def test_xielu_every_bit_pattern(dtype: torch.dtype) -> None:
+    x = torch.arange(-32768, 32768, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    x = x.to(torch.int16).view(dtype)
+    _assert_matches(xielu(x, COEFFS), xielu_reference(x, COEFFS))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("offset", [1, 2, 3, 4, 8])
+def test_xielu_misaligned_views(offset: int) -> None:
+    base = (torch.randn(4 * 21504 + 16, device="cuda") * 3).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    x = base[offset : offset + 2 * 21504]
+    _assert_matches(xielu(x, COEFFS), xielu_reference(x, COEFFS))
+
+
+def test_xielu_special_values() -> None:
+    eps = COEFFS[3].item()
+    vals = [0.0, -0.0, eps, 2 * eps, 1e-38, -1e-38, 3e38, -3e38]
+    vals += [88.0, -88.0, float("inf"), float("-inf"), float("nan")]
+    x = torch.tensor(vals * 3, device="cuda").to(torch.bfloat16)
+    _assert_matches(xielu(x, COEFFS), xielu_reference(x, COEFFS))
+
+
+def test_xielu_out_param_and_empty() -> None:
+    x = torch.randn(3, 21504, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    out = torch.empty_like(x)
+    assert xielu(x, COEFFS, out=out).data_ptr() == out.data_ptr()
+    _assert_matches(out, xielu_reference(x, COEFFS))
+    empty = torch.empty(0, 21504, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    assert xielu(empty, COEFFS).shape == empty.shape
+
+
+def test_xielu_cuda_graph_follows_coefficient_updates() -> None:
+    """The kernel reads the coefficients on device, so a captured graph sees an
+    in-place update (as after a weight update) without recapture."""
+    coeffs = COEFFS.clone()
+    x = torch.randn(16, 21504, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    xielu(x, coeffs)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        out = xielu(x, coeffs)
+    x.copy_(torch.randn_like(x) * 3)
+    graph.replay()
+    _assert_matches(out, xielu_reference(x, coeffs))
+    coeffs.copy_(torch.tensor([0.32, 0.51, 0.5, -1e-6], device="cuda"))
+    graph.replay()
+    _assert_matches(out, xielu_reference(x, coeffs))
+
+
+def _layer(alpha_p: float, alpha_n: float) -> XIELU:
+    layer = XIELU().cuda()
+    layer.alpha_p.data.fill_(alpha_p)
+    layer.alpha_n.data.fill_(alpha_n)
+    layer.update_coefficients()
+    return layer
+
+
+def test_xielu_layer_uses_loaded_coefficients() -> None:
+    """The layer derives the coefficients from the loaded weights, and its CUDA and
+    native paths agree bit for bit."""
+    layer = _layer(166.0, 40.75)
+    expected = xielu_coeffs(layer.alpha_p, layer.alpha_n, layer.beta, layer.eps)
+    assert torch.equal(layer._coeffs, expected)
+    x = (torch.randn(64, 21504, device="cuda") * 3).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    ref = xielu_reference(x, expected)
+    _assert_matches(layer.forward_cuda(x), ref)
+    _assert_matches(layer.forward_native(x), ref)
+    # A non-contiguous input takes the native path and gives the same result.
+    xt = x.t()
+    _assert_matches(layer.forward_cuda(xt), layer.forward_native(xt))
+
+
+def test_xielu_layer_float32_uses_native_path() -> None:
+    layer = _layer(5.5625, 2.359375)
+    x = torch.randn(8, 21504, device="cuda")
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        layer.forward_cuda(x), layer.forward_native(x), rtol=0, atol=0
+    )
+
+
+def test_xielu_layer_builds_on_meta_device() -> None:
+    """Zero-copy IPC loading builds the model on the meta device."""
+    with torch.device("meta"):
+        layer = XIELU()
+    assert layer._coeffs.is_meta
+    assert "_coeffs" not in layer.state_dict()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v", "-s"]))
